title: Above-level text when read aloud
statement: A text read aloud in full may sit above the learners' reading level, up to what they understand by listening, so decoding doesn't cap what they learn.
example: One review let a 35-word sentence stand above the Grade 3 band, recording a note instead of a failure, because every passage was fully voiced.
detail: A Grade 3 review criterion lets read-aloud and think-aloud texts sit above the decoding band at listening-comprehension level, so that knowledge-building is not capped by decoding, and names the IES guide on improving reading comprehension in kindergarten to grade 3 as its source. A simulated review applied it to a 35-word sentence in a story passage and recorded a note rather than a failure, because all passages carried full voiceovers.
against: A blocking row of the course's quality checklist requires "Every passage slice inside the teaching band" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, line 64) and names no exception for text that is read aloud.
